title: Coil-built conical tumbler set
subtitle: A set of three tapered drinking cups, hand-built without a wheel
excerpt: A conical tumbler has gently tapering walls , wider at the rim than the base , which makes it stable in the hand and straightforward to build with coils. This set of three uses air-dry clay and a simple card template to keep each cup consistent in height and angle.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles. Coil-building is among the oldest ceramic methods; technique references from Encyclopedia Britannica 11th edition (1911) pottery entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: A roll of clay used as the building unit in coil construction; joined and smoothed to build up vessel walls
The stage at which clay holds its shape but is still damp enough to work the surface and blend joins
Fully dried, unfired clay; pale, lightweight, and no longer cool to the touch

content.text: A conical tumbler is a plain tapered cylinder, wider at the mouth than the base.
Coil

building suits this form because each ring of coils can be slightly wider than the last, building the taper naturally. Three cups made together means you can match height, check consistency across the set, and speed up the repetition. No kiln needed.

materials.name: PVA glue diluted 50/50 with water (for sealing)

content.text: Making a card template

Cut a card trapezoid: base edge 7 cm wide, top edge 9 cm wide, height 10 cm. This is the profile of one cup wall. Hold the template against your coil stack as you build to keep each cup to the same angle.
Building the first cup
Roll a slab 6 mm thick and cut a circle 7 cm in diameter for the base. Set it on your work surface.

Roll a coil 1 cm in diameter. Start with 40 cm of coil. Score the perimeter of the base with a needle and apply a thin line of water with a damp sponge. Lay the coil around the base perimeter, cutting it to join neatly at the back. Blend the coil to the base on both sides , inside and outside , with a wooden rib.

Add a second coil on top of the first. Place it very slightly outward of the previous coil , a 3 mm outward step per coil builds the taper. Blend both joins. Hold the card template beside the wall to check the angle.
Continue adding coils, stepping out 3 mm each time, until the wall reaches 10 cm high. You will need six to eight coils depending on their diameter. Blend each join before adding the next coil.
Smooth the outside wall with a damp wooden rib, working in gentle vertical strokes. Smooth the inside wall in the same way. The wall should be 5-6 mm thick after smoothing.
Compress the rim lightly with a damp sponge folded over the edge to round and seal it.
Building cups two and three
Build cups two and three in the same sequence. Check each against the card template and against cup one for height. Minor differences at this stage can be corrected before
leather-hard
stage by pressing or pinching the wall carefully.
Drying and sealing
Allow all three cups to reach
bone-dry

over two to three days. Cover loosely with a cloth for the first 24 hours to slow drying and reduce cracking. Once dry, seal with two coats of 50/50 PVA solution inside and out. The seal makes the surface wipe-clean; air-dry clay is not waterproof and these cups are decorative, not for liquid use.
Variations
Press a simple rope texture into the outside wall with a coil before smoothing for a relief surface.
Make a reverse taper , widest at the base, narrower at the rim , for a stable planter or pen holder.
After sealing and drying, paint with acrylic and seal with a matte varnish for a coloured matching set.
Troubleshooter

items.cause: Joins were not blended thoroughly , the coil sat on top of the previous coil rather than being worked in
items.fix: At leather-hard, dampen the crack, score both sides, apply slip, and blend again with a wooden rib

items.problem: Taper is inconsistent across the three cups
items.cause: Each ring of coils was placed at a different step-out, or the card template was not checked consistently
items.fix: At leather-hard, press the wall inward gently at the widest point or add a thin patch of clay to a narrower section, blended in with a damp rib

items.problem: Base has lifted from the floor on drying
items.cause: The base circle dried slower than the walls, causing differential shrinkage
items.fix: Dry on a plaster bat or absorbent board. If the base has lifted, press flat at leather-hard while the clay is still pliable, and support underneath overnight
